model_roles.embedder: chromadb DefaultEmbeddingFunction: all-MiniLM-L6-v2 ONNX (chroma-onnx-models onnx.tar.gz, sha256 913d7300ceae3b2dbc2c50d1de4baacab4be7b9380491c27fab7418616a16ec3), baked into the image

recipe.notes: The vendor's no-LLM benchmark modes. Both benchmark scripts build each palace with chromadb directly (`client.create_collection('mempal_drawers')`, no embedding_function, so ChromaDB's default all-MiniLM-L6-v2 and its default l2 space), the same model mempalace's own `minilm` default wraps (embedding.py; the image build checks the two give the same vector). `raw` is the vendor's default `--mode raw`; `hybrid` is locomo_bench.py `--mode hybrid` without `--llm-rerank`. No LLM is called on ingest or retrieval, so this config makes zero provider calls.

common.notes: Not built. The system has no extraction model, and this bundle runs only the local-embedder benchmark modes; the shim refuses SHIM_CONFIG=common at start. mempalace 3.10.0 can send embeddings to an OpenAI-compatible endpoint (embedding_model openai-compat), which a later common arm could route through the proxy.

time_notes: event_time is stored as the drawer's `timestamp` metadata, where the vendor benchmark stores the session date, and returned as each item's valid_from. The drawer text carries no date (the vendor's session document has none), and neither recipe reads a reference date, so query_time is ignored.

provenance.mechanism: one drawer per session whose ChromaDB id is the session's source_id; every item is one whole drawer, so it cites exactly that session

delete_notes: ChromaDB `collection.delete(ids=[source_id])` on the session's drawer, then `collection.get(ids=[source_id])` confirms it is gone. Nothing is derived across drawers, so no residue is expected.
readiness: synchronous: ChromaDB embeds and indexes each drawer inside `upsert`, so /ingest returns after the write is searchable and /finish only reports the drawer count
namespace: palace: one ChromaDB PersistentClient per namespace at /data/palaces/<ns>/palace, collection mempal_drawers

vendor-default.maps_to: collection.query(query_texts=[question], n_results=10): locomo_bench.py's default --mode raw and --top-k 10 (session granularity). `--policy-setting recipe=hybrid` runs the vendor's hybrid recipe at the same k: query 3k candidates, then fused = distance * (1 - 0.50 * predicate-keyword overlap) * (1 - 0.60 * quoted-phrase hits) * (1 - 0.20 * person-name hits), keep the top k

fixed-evidence.maps_to: the same call with n_results=50 (the vendor's documented --top-k 50 run and longmemeval_bench.py's 50-candidate pool), so the harness packer, not the vendor cutoff, decides what fits the evidence budget; recipe=hybrid queries 150 candidates and keeps 50

recipes.raw: vector search only: the vendor's headline no-LLM mode
recipes.hybrid: locomo_bench.py --mode hybrid with the LLM reranker off: vector candidates re-ranked by keyword, quoted-phrase and person-name boosts

agent_surface.version: mempalace 3.10.0 ships an MCP server (mempalace-mcp); it is not wired here, because the shim builds palaces with the benchmark's ChromaDB calls rather than the mempalace miner

deviations_from_vendor_code: Sessions arrive one at a time through /ingest and are upserted into a persistent palace per namespace; the vendor builds one palace per conversation from all sessions in one add call and deletes it afterwards. Both insert in session order; HNSW search is approximate, so batching could change near-ties at the margin.
Drawer ids are the opaque source ids (src-...) instead of doc_<i>, and the corpus_id metadata is the source id instead of session_<n>, so no dataset identity crosses the sanitizer.
The timestamp metadata is the ISO event_time; the vendor copies LoCoMo's raw date string. Neither recipe reads it.

Every dataset uses the LoCoMo session document (every turn as `Speaker said, "text"`). longmemeval_bench.py indexes user turns only, joined by newlines; the shim cannot tell datasets apart, so it keeps all turns, which also lets questions about what the assistant said find their session.

The hybrid recipe is locomo_bench.py's (predicate keywords 0.50, quoted phrases 0.60, person names 0.20 over 3k candidates). longmemeval_bench.py's hybrid modes (v1 to v4: keyword weight 0.30, question-date boosts, assistant-reference two-pass, synthetic preference drawers, and v4's three fixes tuned on named LongMemEval misses) are not run, because they depend on LongMemEval's question_date format and question wording.

The scoring loop in run_benchmark is re-implemented in shim.py with the vendor's constants; the corpus builder, keyword, quoted-phrase and person-name helpers and the query call are the vendor's own functions, imported from the pinned locomo_bench.py.
The embedder is baked into the image at build time and the container runs with no route to the internet; the vendor downloads it on first use.
